problem:
Consider the line $y=-1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=-8.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the line $y=2$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=14.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=2$ passes through the points $P(0,2)$ and $Q(1,2)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${P}^{′}(2,4)$ and ${Q}^{′}(4,1).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${P}^{′}$ and ${Q}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =\frac{1-4}{4-2}(x-2) \\ y-4 & =-\frac{3}{2}(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-4 & =-\frac{3}{2}(x-2) \\ 2y-8 & =-3x+6 \\ 3x+2y & =14\end{aligned}
$$
